properties.title: Intervention-Conditioned Counterfactual Human Digital Twin Generator

membership.reason: CHDT is an intervention-conditioned autoregressive longitudinal generator simulating complete future multimodal patient-state trajectories under alternative treatment policies.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 action-conditioned longitudinal world model (WT_EHR; downgraded from L3 because Placebo/Statin evaluations are separate held-out arm fidelity checks rather than matched same-patient action comparisons).

properties.backbone: Factual history encoder + LSTM counterfactual autoregressive decoder with irregular-time conditioning and 2-stage cross-mediator refinement

properties.flow: Observed history F_b + static s + irregular intervals Delta t + treatment policy pi -> Monte Carlo autoregressive rollouts of full ICS X^pi_{b+1:t}

properties.purpose: In silico clinical trial simulation and intervention-conditioned dementia trajectory estimation.
properties.environment: Retrospective ADNI cohort and ALPACA synthetic cohorts

assertions.rationale: Explicit elapsed visit intervals Delta t = {delta t_1, delta t_2, ...} conditioned during autoregressive rollout.
Factual encoder embedding multimodal history, static characteristics s, and elapsed intervals.
Autoregressive Integrated Clinical State (ICS) X_i = <M_i, A_i, Y_i> rolled forward over multiple visits.
Conditioned on factual history F_b and previously generated ICSs H^pi_{k-1}.

Reported intervention-conditioned evaluations test separate held-out Placebo (ADNI n=443, ALPACA n=2,000) and Statin (ADNI n=1,654, ALPACA n=2,000) arms under their respective recorded policies rather than comparing two alternative actions applied to the same initial patient history.
Sequential multi-step autoregressive rollout over visits b+1:t.
Learned LSTM encoder-decoder with two-stage cross-mediator refinement.

Future mediator and outcome distributions are conditioned on intervention policy pi and empirically evaluated on held-out Placebo and Statin arms across RIS, SIS, R2S, and S2R settings (Tables 1-2, 4-5; Figures 2-4).
Monte Carlo trajectory sampling (J rollouts) with stochastic noise and Gaussian/softmax heads.

Autoregressive future-state prediction is evaluated across horizons 1-4 on ADNI and ALPACA, achieving horizon-1 normalized RMSE 0.179 vs GNET 0.183 and Total RMSE 0.185 vs 0.194 (p < 0.01, Table 3), plus 1-step through 4-step Macro F1 and Dementia F1 (Tables 4-5).
In silico clinical trial treatment-arm simulation and longitudinal trajectory estimation.
Multi-horizon factual and counterfactual Macro/Micro F1 across horizons 1-4 (RIS) and 1-9 (SIS).
Placebo vs Statin treatment-arm counterfactual evaluation on ALPACA and empirical support plausibility checks; authors note indirect counterfactual evidence.
Cross-source robustness across Real-to-Synthetic (R2S) and Synthetic-to-Real (S2R) ADNI/ALPACA shifts.

evidence_fragments.content: To address these challenges, we propose CHDT, an intervention-conditioned Human Digital Twin generator for long-term multimodal trajectory estimation and in silico treatment-arm simulation.

CHDT consists of an encoder and a decoder, as shown in Figure 1. Factual encoder: encodes the observed patient history, static characteristics, and elapsed time intervals into a latent representation. Counterfactual decoder: sequentially generates ICSs conditioned on the observed history and previously generated ICSs given stochastic noise. The decoder uses prior heads to model dependencies among mediators and produce the final predictive distributions.

The overall robustness summary in Figure 2 is consistent with this favorable later-horizon performance across factual and counterfactual evaluations. Agreement with observed ADNI treatment-arm outcomes provides an indirect fidelity check rather than direct validation of individual counterfactual trajectories.
these analyses provide indirect counterfactual evidence rather than direct validation of individual potential outcomes.
We assess intervention-conditioned fidelity by comparing generated trajectories with held-out observed treatment arms. These evaluations provide indirect counterfactual checks.

As shown in Table 3, CHDT achieves a lower Total RMSE than GNET (0.185 vs. 0.194; p <0.01) and consistently lower errors across horizons 1–4 (0.179–0.210 vs. 0.183–0.216), indicating more accurate and stable autoregressive trajectory generation.

Each cohort comprises Development, Placebo, and Statin arms. The Development arm is divided into training, validation, and factual test subsets (80/10/10), while Placebo and Statin are reserved for counterfactual evaluation.

capability_assessments.rationale: Downgraded honestly from L3 to L2: CHDT implements persistent state (019), temporal autoregressive dynamics (041), and learned LSTM transition with cross-mediator refinement (042), and evaluates action-conditioned multi-step rollouts (043, 053) across ADNI and ALPACA Placebo and Statin arms. However, reported intervention-conditioned evaluations test separate held-out Placebo and Statin cohorts (arm-level fidelity checks) rather than matched paired alternative-action comparisons on the same initial patient histories (action.comparison absent), so L3 is not established.

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R2 Retrospective cohort and simulator validation

limitations: Counterfactual interpretation relies on untestable causal assumptions (consistency, sequential exchangeability, positivity).
Cross-mediator refinement captures conditional dependence rather than structural causal graphs.
Indirect counterfactual evidence only; no prospective clinical trial validation.

Intervention-conditioned evaluations assess separate held-out Placebo and Statin cohorts rather than matched alternative-action trajectories from the same initial patient histories (supporting L2 rather than L3).

legacy_cells.B: An Intervention-Conditioned Human Digital Twin Generator for In Silico Clinical Trial Simulation
legacy_cells.C: Saeed Farzi; Sofia Michopoulou; Christopher Kipps; Rahman Attar
legacy_cells.O: Dementia, including mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease progression
legacy_cells.S: Generate future multimodal clinical-state trajectories for dementia patients under specified statin or placebo treatment policies.
legacy_cells.T: ADNI: Development 4,103 patients (2,391 normal, 1,292 MCI, 420 dementia), Placebo 443, Statin 1,654; ALPACA: 2,000 patients per arm.
legacy_cells.AI: Longitudinal clinical and demographic data; cognitive assessments; CSF biomarkers; MRI-derived volumes; visit-level medication/treatment exposure; elapsed visit intervals; static patient characteristics
legacy_cells.AJ: Recurrent LSTM encoder/decoder; encoder may also be recurrent or transformer-based, but the study implementation uses LSTM.
legacy_cells.AM: Encoder combines observed history, static patient characteristics, and elapsed intervals into a shared latent representation; decoder generates mediator and outcome states.
legacy_cells.BD: Statin exposure recorded at each visit; future medication use is not used to label earlier treatment states.
legacy_cells.BS: Autoregressively generated multimodal future patient-state trajectories, comprising mediator and outcome states under an intervention policy.
legacy_cells.BT: Mediator-specific and outcome heads; softmax for categorical outputs and regression or Gaussian heads for continuous outputs.
legacy_cells.BV: Continuous variables: mean squared error or Gaussian negative log-likelihood; categorical/binary variables: cross-entropy; total loss combines continuous and categorical losses.
legacy_cells.CV: Consistency; sequential exchangeability conditional on observed history; positivity/treatment overlap. These assumptions are stated, not established by observational fit.
legacy_cells.DQ: ADNI: 4,103 Development patients, 443 Placebo patients, and 1,654 Statin patients; ALPACA: 2,000 patients per arm.
legacy_cells.DX: Normalized RMSE, horizon 1: CHDT 0.179 vs GNET 0.183; Table 4 also reports one-step Macro F1 for RIS settings.
legacy_cells.DY: Normalized RMSE by horizon: CHDT 0.179, 0.174, 0.185, 0.210 at horizons 1–4; total 0.185 vs GNET 0.194 (p < 0.01).
legacy_cells.EA: Propensity-score support check used overlap threshold α = 0.2; most generated trajectories were above the threshold and in the intermediate overlap region.
legacy_cells.EB: Intervention-conditioned fidelity was assessed separately for Placebo and Statin arms; RIS Placebo Macro F1 decreased from 0.799 at step 1 to 0.557 at step 4.
legacy_cells.ED: Cross-source transfer evaluated in both directions: ADNI-trained models on ALPACA (R2S) and ALPACA-trained models on ADNI (S2R); these are not prospective clinical validation.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with CRN, GTrans, TECDE, RMSN, and GNET; CHDT total normalized RMSE was 0.185 versus GNET 0.194 (p < 0.01).
legacy_cells.EK: Ablated irregular-time modeling (Baseline+T) and cross-mediator modeling (Baseline+C); CHDT combines both. Table 1 reports horizon-1–4 averages across 10 runs.
legacy_cells.EL: CDR-SB was the most challenging feature for both CHDT and GNET; the paper also notes visible CHDT underestimation at horizon 4 in the trajectory visualization.
legacy_cells.FL: Factual encoder embeds observed patient history, static characteristics, and visit gaps into a shared latent representation; an LSTM-based autoregressive counterfactual decoder takes the intervention policy and generates mediator/outcome states using prior and cross-mediator refinement heads. No planning module is described.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces CHDT for intervention-conditioned multimodal patient-state trajectory generation; combines irregular-time autoregressive generation with mediator-specific dependency decomposition; evaluates factual and intervention-conditioned fidelity across real ADNI and simulator-generated ALPACA cohorts.
legacy_cells.FN: In RIS, CHDT had highest mean Macro F1 at three of four factual horizons and highest Dementia F1 at all four; its normalized Macro F1 drop was 13.15% in SIS. For generative evaluation, total normalized RMSE was 0.185 vs GNET 0.194 (p < 0.01).
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state that residual unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded in ADNI and that treatment-arm agreement is an indirect counterfactual check, not direct validation of individual potential outcomes.
legacy_cells.FQ: Prior longitudinal models often focus on outcome/event prediction rather than complete patient-state trajectory generation, and commonly overlook irregular visit intervals and cross-mediator dependencies.
legacy_cells.FR: The evidence is retrospective fidelity/transfer evaluation, not prospective patient benefit or direct validation of individual potential outcomes; real-world ADNI residual unmeasured confounding remains possible. Cross-source tests include simulator-generated ALPACA, not an external clinical cohort.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Pass the paper’s specified action and time context explicitly into the state-transition interface; preserve the boundary between predictive action sensitivity and identified intervention effects.
